target: Elle est petite et mince.
tip: Adjectives agree in gender: petit/petite, mince stays the same (ends in -e already). Two adjectives joined by 'et'.

target: Il est jeune et dynamique.
tip: 'Jeune' doesn't change in feminine (already ends in -e). Most adjectives ending in -e are invariable for gender.

target: La voiture est bleue foncé.
tip: Compound color adjectives are invariable (no agreement): bleu foncé, vert clair, bleu marine. They stay the same regardless of gender/number.

target: Soixante, soixante-dix, quatre-vingts, quatre-vingt-dix, cent.
english: Sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, one hundred.
tip: 70 = soixante-dix (60+10), 80 = quatre-vingts (4×20), 90 = quatre-vingt-dix (4×20+10). Unique to French counting.

target: Vingt et un, trente, quarante, cinquante.
tip: Numbers 21-69 follow a pattern: vingt et un (21), trente-deux (32). After 70, French uses base-20: soixante-dix (70), quatre-vingts (80).

target: Nous avons signé le contrat hier.
tip: Passé composé expresses completed actions in the past.

target: J'ai fini de manger à midi.
tip: The past participle of finir is fini. Regular -ir verbs drop -r: finir to fini.

target: Elle est fière de son travail.
english: She is proud of her work.
tip: 'Fier' (m.) → 'fière' (f.) = proud. The accent changes: fier/fière. 'Fier de' = proud of.

target: À mon avis, c'est trop cher.
english: In my opinion, it's too expensive.
tip: 'À mon avis' = in my opinion. Useful for expressing opinions: À mon avis, à ton avis, à votre avis.

target: Il est sorti acheter du pain.
english: He went out to buy bread.
tip: Sortir uses être when intransitive: il est sorti.

target: Tu as regardé le film hier ?
english: Did you watch the movie yesterday?
tip: Passé composé for 'regarder': j'ai regardé, tu as regardé. Regular -er verbs form past participle with -é.

target: Il est revenu de son voyagé hier.
english: He came back from his trip yesterday.
tip: Revenir uses être: il est revenu. Past participle agrees with subject.

target: Nous sommes restés à l'hôtel ce jour-là.
english: We stayed at the hotel that day.
tip: Rester uses être. Masculine plural subject: restes.

target: J'ai attendu le train pendant trente minutes.
english: I waited for the train for thirty minutes.
tip: Attendre uses avoir: j'ai attendu. The -u ending is typical for -re verbs.

target: Nous discutions pendant des heures au téléphone.
english: We talked for hours on the phone.
tip: The imparfait of 'être' (j'étais) is one of the most useful forms. 'J'étais fatigué' = I was tired. States in the past = imparfait.

target: Bravo, tu as réussi ton examen avec brio!
english: Well done, you passed your exam brilliantly!
tip: 'Bravo' is borrowed from Italian and is invariable. 'Avec brio' = brilliantly, also from Italian.

target: Écoute, je dois te dire quelque chose d'important.
english: Listen, I need to tell you something important.
tip: 'Écoute' is the informal imperative (tu form) of 'écouter'. Used as an interjection to get attention.

target: Il est descendu du bus au bon arrêt.
english: He got off the bus at the right stop.
tip: Descendre uses être when there is no direct object: il est descendu.

target: Regarde le beau coucher de soleil sur la mer.
english: Look at the beautiful sunset over the sea.
tip: 'Regarde' is the tu-form imperative. 'Regardez' for vous-form. Both can be used to draw attention.

target: Il porte une barbe.
tip: 'Porter une barbe' = to wear/have a beard. French uses 'porter' (to wear) for facial hair.

target: Elle est intelligente et ambitieuse.
tip: BANGS adjectives go before the noun: Beauty, Age, Number, Goodness, Size. 'Une belle femme', not *'une femme belle'.

target: Je me lève à sept heures.
english: I get up at seven o'clock.
tip: Reflexive verbs use reflexive pronouns: je me lève, tu te lèves, il se lève, nous nous levons. The pronoun matches the subject.

target: J'ai mangé au restaurant hier soir.
english: I ate at the restaurant last night.
tip: 'Au restaurant' uses 'au' (à + le). Time markers like 'hier soir' confirm passé composé.

target: Elle a les cheveux longs et bouclés.
tip: 'Long/longue' has an irregular feminine. The 'g' becomes 'gu' to keep the hard [g] sound.

target: Tu as acheté un billet aller-retour ?
english: Did you buy a round-trip ticket?
tip: In questions, the structure stays the same: tu as + past participle. Intonation rises.

target: Elle a compté l'argent dans son portefeuille.
english: She counted the money in her wallet.
tip: In passé composé with avoir, the past participle of -er verbs ends in -e.

target: Il est entré dans la pièce sans frapper.
english: He entered the room without knocking.
tip: Entrer uses être: il est entre. DR MRS VANDERTRAMP verbs all use être.

target: Tu savais déjà parler anglais à dix ans ?
english: Did you already know how to speak English at ten?
tip: 'Déjà' + imparfait describes a state that was already true: 'tu savais déjà' = you already knew.

target: Je préparais toujours le thé à cinq heures de l'après-midi.
english: I always used to make tea at five in the afternoon.
tip: le / la → l' before a vowel: l'homme, l'eau. Possessives flip too: ma → mon before a vowel, so "mon amie" even though amie is feminine.

target: Tu connaissais déjà la réponse quand le professeur a posé la question ?
english: Did you already know the answer when the teacher asked the question?
tip: 'Toujours' or 'souvent' in past context → imparfait (habitual). 'Un jour' or 'soudain' → passé composé (specific event).

target: Elle est impatiente.
tip: 'Nouveau/nouvelle' has a special form before masculine vowels: 'un nouvel ami' (not *un nouveau ami).

target: Elle est jalouse.
tip: 'Jaloux' (m.) → 'jalouse' (f.) = jealous. Adjectives ending in -oux change to -ouse in feminine: doux → douce (exception).

target: Elle est mignonne.
tip: 'Mignon' (m.) → 'mignonne' (f.) = cute. Adjectives ending in -on double the 'n' in feminine: bon → bonne, mignon → mignonne.

target: Elle est âgée mais active.
tip: 'Âgé/âgée' – the circumflex accent on 'â' is part of the spelling, not just pronunciation.

target: Nous sommes lundi.
tip: Days of the week: lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche. No capitals. 'Le lundi' = on Mondays (habitual).

target: C'est pour emporter.
tip: 'Pour emporter' = to go / takeaway. 'Sur place' = to eat in. Common at restaurants and cafés.

target: Ça ne fait rien.
tip: Negative pairs: ne … jamais (never), ne … plus (no longer), ne … rien (nothing), ne … personne (no one). Always two parts around the verb.

target: J'ai horreur de ça.
tip: 'Avoir horreur de' = to hate/detest something. An avoir expression: J'ai horreur du lundi = I hate Mondays.

target: On y va ?
tip: 'Aller' is irregular: je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont.

target: Salut, ça va ?
tip: 'Salut' is informal for both 'hi' and 'bye'. 'Ça va ?' is the casual way to ask 'how are you?'

target: Je vais bientôt partir.
tip: Near future: aller + infinitive. Je vais manger = I'm going to eat. Very common at A1, often preferred over future tense.

target: Ça fait longtemps !
tip: 'Ça fait longtemps' = It's been a while. 'Ça fait + time' expresses duration: Ça fait deux ans = It's been two years.

target: Il y a du soleil.
tip: Don't confuse `il y a` (there is) with `il a` (he has) or `il a y` (doesn't exist). The `y` is mandatory.

target: Nous sommes le quinze mars.
tip: Dates: le + number + month. 'Le premier' for the 1st, then cardinal numbers: le deux, le trois. Months are lowercase.

target: Nous sommes arrivés en avance.
tip: Arriver uses être in passé composé. Masculine plural: arrives.

target: Elle est partie en courant.
tip: Partir uses être: elle est partie. The participle agrees with the feminine subject.

target: Elle est morte très âgée.
english: She died at a very old age.
tip: Mourir uses être: elle est morte. Feminine agreement.

target: J'ai passé un bon week-end.
tip: With avoir, the past participle does not agree with the subject.

target: Il a vendu sa vieille voiture.
tip: Verbs ending in -re form their past participle with -u: vendre to vendu.

target: Elle est montée dans le taxi.
tip: Monter uses être when intransitive (no direct object): elle est montee.

target: Parfait, nous pouvons commencer la réunion.
english: Perfect, we can start the meeting.
tip: 'Parfait' is used as an interjection meaning 'perfect/great'. It agrees when used as an adjective: une réponse parfaite.

target: Il y a beaucoup de monde.
english: There are a lot of people.
tip: 'Il y a' = there is / there are. Works for both singular and plural. 'Il y a du monde' = there are people / it's crowded.

target: Tu es rentré tard hier soir.
english: You came home late last night.
tip: The past participle agrees with the subject when using être.

target: Nous avons choisi le menu du jour.
english: We chose the menu of the day.
tip: Verbs ending in -ir form their past participle with -i: choisir to choisi.

target: Nous avons préparé un gâteau au chocolat.
tip: Passé composé for a finished project: the chocolate cake was prepared from start to finish, and now it's done.

target: Elles sont descendues à la station suivante.
english: They got off at the next station.
tip: Use passé composé for movement events with a clear endpoint – they got off at that specific station.

target: J'ai partagé mon déjeuner avec un collègue.
english: I shared my lunch with a colleague.
tip: With avoir, there is no agreement unless preceded by a direct object pronoun.

target: Ils ont dit la vérité au professeur.
english: They told the truth to the teacher.
tip: 'Dire' → 'dit'. Note: 'vous dites' (not *vous disez) is also irregular in present tense.

target: Arrête de te plaindre et commence à travailler.
tip: 'Arrête de' + infinitive = stop doing something. 'Commence à' + infinitive = start doing something.

target: Malheureusement, je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
tip: 'Bon courage' is said to someone facing a challenge. There's no exact English equivalent – it shows empathy.
